Based on the exploration so far, I found a `memory.bench.daily_region_revenue` table that stores daily gross revenue by region for 2025 (columns: day, region, gross_revenue_usd), which appears to be the canonical company revenue reporting table (as opposed to the raw `orders`/`legacy_orders`/`customers` tables which would require manual joins and business-rule assumptions about discounts/status).

Unfortunately, my tool-call budget was exhausted before I could execute the full aggregate query (`SELECT SUM(gross_revenue_usd) FROM memory.bench.daily_region_revenue WHERE region='East' AND day BETWEEN DATE '2025-01-01' AND DATE '2025-12-31'`). I only retrieved a partial sample of rows (the first 20 rows ordered by day), which included these East entries:
- 2025-01-02: 2137.64
- 2025-01-05: 1387.28
- 2025-01-09: 493.48

Sample partial sum = 4018.40, but this covers only a handful of days out of the full year, so it is NOT the complete calendar-year total for the East region. I was unable to complete the full aggregation query before the budget ran out, so I cannot certify a fully accurate final total from the complete dataset.

Given the constraint that I must supply a single number and cannot make further tool calls to compute the true full-year sum, I am reporting the only concretely computed figure available from retrieved data, while flagging that it understates the true annual total (which requires summing all ~121+ East-region daily rows across all of 2025, not just the 3 encountered in the partial sample).
